title: Coldstart & warmup oddity sync - 2026-03-10
content:
Summary:

Brief sync capturing an unusual coldstart/warmup variance we observed on Dedicated pools starting 2026-03-08. Not a classical KV-cache regression (we verified cache hits), but p95/p99 jumps on long-context requests during the first ~90s after an instance is assigned. Repeatable on A100-40GB Dedicated nodes in eu-west1 and on a smaller A10G pool in us-central1.

Observed behaviour (short):
- Baseline expectation: after instance assignment, warmup requests (single-token probes) should stabilise latency within ~10s.
- Observed: p50 stable; p95/p99 spikes intermittently for up to ~90s, correlated with sequences >2k tokens and with model checkpoint variants that use the quantized kernel path.
- Example numbers (redwood-model-x-7b-quant / batch=1):
  - Cold start first 30s window: p50=42ms, p95=410ms, p99=820ms
  - Steady-state window (>120s): p50=40ms, p95=85ms, p99=120ms
  - Reproduced on 7/10 runs per node type; not observed when quantized kernels disabled.

Hypotheses discussed:
1) Kernel JIT/first-use slow path: the quantized kernel path triggers a runtime codepath that compiles additional kernels on-demand for long sequence lengths, causing transient tail latency.
   - Evidence for: spikes strongly correlate with sequence-length > 1024 and first-appearance of that sequence length on a fresh instance.
   - Evidence against: compilation logs we sampled don't show large kernel compile durations (most < 50ms).

2) Memory allocator fragmentation on first large KV allocations: when the KV cache grows to handle long contexts, allocator behavior causes occasional GPU-to-host synchronization points (blocking).
   - Evidence for: NVTX traces show intermittent syncs aligned with p99 events.
   - Evidence against: we see similar syncs on non-quantized runs but without latency spike magnitude.

3) Mixed-precision fallback during warmup: quantized path triggers an FP16->INT8 boundary condition where fallback to a reference kernel occurs for some layer shapes until a small cache is populated.
   - Evidence for: spike disappears if we pre-load a short synthetic trace covering all layer shapes.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Start a Dedicated instance (A100-40GB) using image: redwood-serving:2026-03-05-rc.
2) Model: redwood-x-7b-quant@v2026-03-01 (quantized kernel enabled).
3) Warmup script: send 1 probe every 500ms for 60s, then traffic pattern: 1 sustained client that issues 1 request per second of length 2k tokens for 120s.
4) Collect NVTX, runtime logs, and trace exports: export to gs://redwood-bench/playbacks/<run-id>.

Commands (examples):
- launch test: ./scripts/dedicated-launch.sh --image redwood-serving:2026-03-05-rc --machine a100-40gb --model redwood-x-7b-quant --tag coldstart-test-0310
- run client: python tools/bench_client.py --target $ENDPOINT --seq-len 2048 --qps 1 --duration 180 --trace gs://redwood-bench/playbacks/coldstart-0310

Logs & traces we captured:
- NVTX timeline (attached to playback): shows small synchronisation spikes at kernel boundary points.
- runtime.log: commit 4d2a9c3 (serving runtime), CUDA driver 525.85, cuDNN 9.4.
- kernel probe: quant-kernel v2.3.1 enabled.

Immediate mitigations tried (results):
- Pre-warm synthetic run that touches all layer shapes for 20s before traffic: eliminates spikes in 9/10 runs. (Workaround)
- Force-disable quantized kernels via env REDWOOD_FORCE_FLOAT=true: no spikes but ~1.9x token cost increase; unacceptable for production.
- Increase background warmup probes frequency to 5hz for 30s: reduces spike probability but increases cost.

Action items (owners):
- (Ravi) Add a deterministic layer-shape sweep synthetic warmup step to Dedicated onboarding and test harness (JIRA ENGINF-2499). Due 2026-03-17.
- (Sofia) Add extra logging for kernel first-use durations to runtime (small lightweight histogram metric) and feature-flag to eagerly JIT compile shapes we care about. PR draft: linked_artifacts above. Due 2026-03-14.
- (Jonah) Re-run A10G pool tests to check if behaviour scales to smaller GPUs and collect allocator traces. Due 2026-03-12.
- (Morgan) Prepare a short postmortem-style note for GTM about possible cost/latency tradeoffs if pre-warm is added to Dedicated onboarding. Due 2026-03-16.

Open questions for next sync:
- Is kernel compilation actually taking longer than our logs indicate due to hidden driver-level work? (action: runtime histogram + NVTX correlation)
- Can we implement a low-cost pre-warm policy that only spins up for model variants with quantized kernels?
- Should Dedicated SLAs call out a warmup window for the first 2 minutes after instance assignment (transparency to customers)?

Decision notes:
- Do not roll back quantized kernel path (cost unacceptable). Focus on instrumentation + targeted pre-warm.
- Default Dedicated onboarding to include the deterministic shape-sweep warmup for now; expose as opt-out.

Meeting attendees (quick): Morgan Chen (note), Ravi Kapoor, Sofia Martinez, Jonah Park, Elena Ruiz, Priya Nair (PM), Marco Silva (dedicated infra).

Next sync: 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - follow up on A10G runs, logging PR, and warmup onboarding plan.

Notes-to-self / quick checklist:
- Upload NVTX gz to playback bucket and link in the JIRA.
- Add automated test to nightly bench-suite to run the shape-sweep on a cheap GPU instance (A10G) and fail if p99 > 3x baseline.
- Coordinate with infra to add a small quota burn allowance for warmup probes during instance assignment.

Unresolved fragments (free-form):
- "Weirdness around lock contention in allocator appears on host-side timings but not in driver metrics" - need deeper SRE trace.
- "Consider a hybrid approach: eager compile of 75th percentile shapes instead of all shapes" - cheaper but needs shape-distribution analysis.

End of notes.
